newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Oct industrial output up 15.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Oct industrial output up 15.5 pct.

text.p: Mexico's industrial activity in October rose 15.5 percent, the second highest monthly gain in the year, with increases occuring across the board, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) said on Monday.

The rise was higher than a 10.65 percent average forecast in a Reuters survey. INEGI said the September increase was revised to 13.7 percent from 14 percent. In the first 10 months of the year, the accumulated rise in output was up 10.3 percent.

In a breakdown of the October 1996 versus October 1995 data, INEGI said mining was up 24.7 percent, with the oil-related sub-division up 45 percent and non-oil up 2.9 percent. The oil-related rise was bolstered by a comparison with last year when Hurricane Roxanne disrupted oil activity in Campeche state.

Manufacturing activity was up 14.5 percent, leading to a rise of 11.2 percent in the first 10 months of the year. In the January-October period, maquiladora output grew 17.9 percent, while non-maquila production rose 10.8 percent.
Construction activity in October rose 22.6 percent, or 9.4 percent in the January to October period.
Generation of electricity, gas and water climbed 4.8 percent in October, and 4.3 percent between January and October, compared with the same periods the previous year.
